prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: native DFU pixel-art eye-gaze atlas for one angry expression
Primary request: Edit the supplied 3x3 reference grid into nine anatomically coherent gaze directions for this same pixel-art woman.
Input images: Image 1 is the exact angry-expression 3x3 upper-face reference atlas. Use it as identity, palette, face-framing, and current-expression source.
Composition/framing: Return only the complete 3x3 atlas, 1536x840 pixels if possible, with nine equal 512x280 cells and no gutters, labels, borders, or text. Each cell represents one native 64x35 upper portrait. Row-major direction order: TOP-LEFT, UP, TOP-RIGHT / LEFT, STRAIGHT AHEAD, RIGHT / BOTTOM-LEFT, DOWN, BOTTOM-RIGHT. Keep both pupils aimed together in every cell. Make every row visibly distinct vertically; diagonals must include clear vertical and horizontal gaze components.
Subject: Same angry woman in all cells. Preserve her exact angry brow expression and tension in every cell: keep brow angle, pinch, darkness, creases, eye spacing, socket shape, skin, hair, background, and face identity. Do not soften her brows or face into neutral or happy expression.
Style/medium: Match reference low-resolution softly shaded pixel art and square pixel lattice.
Eye anatomy: Redraw each iris, pupil, eye opening, and lids as one coherent eye. For UP and upper diagonals, raise each upper eyelid naturally and open the eye enough to make room for the elevated iris and pupil inside the eyeball opening. Keep both irises compact and visibly inside the opening; never place an iris on the lid or skin. Use modest widening only, not a startled look or giant white eyes. For DOWN and lower diagonals, lower the gaze within a naturally lowered upper lid; let lids correctly occlude the iris. Allow natural lower-lid adjustment. Keep eye corners and spacing stable. Permit lid contours to follow each gaze. Do not force a fixed slit or fixed iris rectangle. Do not move the eye sockets or eyebrows to fake gaze.
Palette: Compact muted violet-gray irises; tiny restrained highlights; warm subdued sclera; original warm brown skin and dark brown brows. No bright-white crescents, round vector pupils, giant doll eyes, or palette drift.
Center match: The middle-center straight-ahead cell should retain the reference's original angry eye appearance as closely as possible. Preserve all non-eye pixels in every cell from the reference.
Avoid: Repeating the center gaze in other cells, reversing vertical direction, severed irises, pupils embedded in eyelids, exaggerated surprise, neutral/happy brows, new objects, extra characters, text, or watermark.
